sources.citation: A US maker's public NM-B product sheet (rev. 03/2019, read; it carries no ampacity column), paraphrased: NM-B 12/2 with ground is listed to UL 719, its insulated conductors to UL 83 (both by number); 2 insulated 12 AWG copper conductors (solid) laid parallel with a bare 12 AWG copper grounding conductor wrapped in paper, the assembly wrapped in a paper separator under a PVC jacket. The conductor entries are pinned (the sorrelby-nm and sorrelby-bare entries). Roles and colours: white is the grounded conductor (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 200.6), the bare conductor is the EGC (Art. 250.119), both by number; black for the ungrounded conductor is convention, not code. The order (ungrounded, grounded, EGC) is save format. NM-B's 60 °C ampacity limit (Art. 334.80, by number) is a P4 rule; no ampacity is stored.

The jacket is PVC applied over the whole assembly (the same sheet): the pinned insulation row nmbJacket, whose 90 °C is the conductors' rating; NM cable is for dry locations only (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 334.12, by number).

Jacket colour by conductor size, a convention shared across makers' NM-B lines and shown on the same sheet: white for 14 AWG, yellow for 12 AWG, orange for 10 AWG, black for 8 and 6 AWG; this cable is 12 AWG, so yellow. Some makers colour three-conductor cable differently; this catalogue uses the size colour for both (a game-design choice between real schemes).

The same sheet's approximate cable dimension for 12/2, flat, about 0.200 × 0.400 in, converted at 25.4 mm/in and rounded to 0.01 mm (height the minor axis, width the major). It includes the paper wraps the model doesn't carry. Paraphrased per entry; no table copied.

game-design: a 0.762 mm (30 mil) PVC jacket wall. Makers' NM-B sheets commonly state 25 to 30 mil, but the sheets seen that state it also carry ampacity columns (NEC table reprints), so none is cited; the sheet read gives none.
